sections.content:
87,925 people

were counted on the census as "senior care workers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Senior care workers routinely oversee and monitor care workers, care assistants and home carers.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "senior care workers" there were more women than men (84.2% compared with 15.8%).

This means "senior care workers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 15.8% and women made up 84.2% of "senior care workers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "senior care workers" included:

  • pharmaceutical technicians
  • primary education teaching professionals
  • company secretaries and administrators

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "senior care workers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "senior care workers", 13.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "senior care workers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "senior care workers" included:

  • business associate professionals (other)
  • office supervisors
  • electronics engineers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "senior care workers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "senior care workers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "senior care workers", 13.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (77.3% compared with 22.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.1%) than self-employed (0.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
